Bug_Title: ICAST: int value cast to float and then passed to Math.round (ICAST_INT_CAST_TO_FLOAT_PASSED_TO_ROUND)
Bug_Details:
This code converts an int value to a float precision
floating point number and then
passing the result to the Math.round() function, which returns the int/long closest
to the argument. This operation should always be a no-op,
since converting an integer to a float should give a number with no fractional part.
It is likely that the operation that generated the value to be passed
to Math.round was intended to be performed using
floating point arithmetic.
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates the bug by casting an int value to a float and then passing it to Math.round, which is unnecessary as the input is already an integer and the float conversion adds no fractional part. This operation is effectively a no-op.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with an integer input, causing unnecessary casting from int to float and then rounding. The assertEquals checks the result against the original integer, expecting the same value, but the test will fail due to the float casting and rounding process.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that both tests passed successfully, as shown by the 'OK (2 tests)' result. This confirms that the bug was not triggered, as the assertions did not fail.
